statement: An integer primary key routes by numeric order against the text boundary the partitions system table hands back after a split: one comparator, compareRoutingKeys in src/partition/split-key-comparator.js (the typed split-key owner), decides routing order for KeyRange.compareKeys, PartitionResolver.compareValues and LiveQueryGroup.compareValues, compares a number against a text-encoded number numerically, keeps string-against-string and number-against-number order unchanged, and refuses any other mixed key space with the typed split-key mismatch outcome instead of String coercion; and every entry of every vocabulary in src/query/query-constants.js has a consumer, the dead entries being removed rather than exported for documentation.

constraints.statement: One red test file for routing, one census test for the vocabulary, the three call sites delegating to the one owner, and the dead entries deleted; no log adapter, no message group, no split workflow behaviour beyond the comparator, so the quest is safe alongside the running soak.

A mixed key space that is not a number against a text-encoded number is a typed outcome (the split-key mismatch the owner already raises), never a String comparison; the text-encoded number case exists only because partition_key_start/end are TEXT columns, and it is named as such in the owner.
String-against-string order stays localeCompare and number-against-number stays numeric, so no string-keyed table changes partition.
The src/ change lands only behind an independent verification newer than the last attempt.
